acceptance_condition: A study with ground-truth tasks, mixed-capability LLM agents at varied majority/minority and capability configurations, measuring both answer-shift rates (conformity) and group accuracy pre/post exposure, under matched total inference compute.
rationale: Choi's topics are deliberately ground-truth-free, so its conformity rates measure persuasion, not accuracy. The note's mechanism needs to know whether the capability-dominance effect (one strong agent outweighs a majority) is error-correcting (strong agent is right and pulls the group toward truth) or error-amplifying (strong agent is confidently wrong and collapses diversity) on verifiable tasks - this determines whether staged retrieval should amplify or dampen high-capability voices.
text: Do Choi-style conformity dynamics - majority pull dominated by single high-capability agents, and minority capitulation - reproduce on tasks with verifiable ground truth, and when they occur, do they reduce or increase aggregate error relative to independent sampling?
